weaknesses: The abstract makes overly broad claims about the superiority of Neural Quadratic Models (NQMs) without sufficient empirical backing.
The experimental setup lacks a comprehensive comparison with existing models beyond just NQMs and linear models, limiting the contextual understanding of performance.
Key assumptions regarding the generalizability of results across different architectures and tasks are not adequately justified.
The paper does not sufficiently address the limitations of NQMs or the conditions under which they may fail to outperform traditional models.
strengths: The introduction of Neural Quadratic Models (NQMs) provides a novel perspective on understanding neural network dynamics, particularly in the context of large learning rates.
The theoretical analysis of the catapult phase is well-articulated, offering significant insights into optimization dynamics that are not captured by linear models.
The empirical results demonstrate a clear correlation between the theoretical predictions and the observed behaviors of NQMs, supporting the proposed framework.
The paper effectively highlights the limitations of existing linear approximations, thereby establishing a strong case for the relevance of NQMs in future AI research.
